title: Primate Hair Cortisol Processing
author: Kimberley A Phillips
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bw8wphxe

steps.title: Collect Hair Samples
steps.instruction: Collect hair samples from the upper back of the animal, ensuring consistency in body region across all animals in the study.

substeps.instruction: Clean electric clippers with alcohol before and after use.
Shave hair close to the skin using electric clippers, avoiding nicks to prevent blood contamination.
Wrap the distal end of each sample in masking tape, leaving 1–1.5 cm of the proximal hair exposed.
Place samples in envelopes labeled with species name, subject ID, sex, DOB, DOC, location of hair sample, and project affiliation code.
Store envelopes at -20 °C (-4 °F) or room temperature out of direct sunlight.

steps.title: Prepare Sample Weighing Materials
steps.instruction: Prepare the paper and labels required for weighing the hair samples.

substeps.instruction: Clean forceps and spatula with isopropyl alcohol wipes before and after use.
Cut a 7cm x 7cm square of printer paper for each sample.
Create 4–5 labels for each sample using the information from the envelope labels.
Weigh the 7cm x 7cm paper on an analytical scale, record the weight, and tare the scale.

steps.title: Trim and Weigh Hair
steps.instruction: Isolate the specific hair segment for analysis and record its weight.

substeps.instruction: Wearing laboratory gloves, remove the hair sample from the container and identify the shaved end.
Using scissors and a ruler, cut 1-1.5cm of hair from the exposed proximal end.
Transfer the cut hair onto the square paper and record the weight.

steps.title: Wash Hair Samples
steps.instruction: Clean the hair samples using HPLC grade isopropanol.

substeps.instruction: Transfer hair into a 15 mL polypropylene tube and affix the subject label.
Use a motorized pipette controller and 10 mL serological pipette to add 5 mL of HPLC grade isopropanol.
Invert the sample on a rotator at speed 12 for 3 minutes.
Decant the isopropanol into a waste container using a glass funnel, using a spatula to catch any hair traveling down the tube.
Repeat the washing (addition of isopropanol, rotation, and decanting) two more times.

steps.title: Dry and Pulverize Hair
steps.instruction: Completely dry the hair and grind it into a fine powder.

substeps.instruction: Place tubes on a rack in a fume hood with lids off to dry for 4-5 days.
Separate each dried hair sample in half and place each half into a mill jar.
Grind hair to a fine powder using a ball mill for 6 minutes at 25 Hz.
Scrape the sides of the jar with a spatula to collect all powdered hair.

steps.title: Aliquot Powdered Hair
steps.instruction: Weigh the required amount of powdered hair into microcentrifuge tubes.

substeps.instruction: Affix a sample ID label to a 2 mL microcentrifuge tube, weigh the tube, and tare.
Clean forceps with isopropanol before use.
Transfer the required amount of powder into the tube: 50mg (0.05g) for Capuchins, marmosets, and tamarins; 40mg (0.04g) for Chimpanzees.
Store any remaining powdered hair in another labeled 2 mL microcentrifuge tube in the refrigerator or at room temperature.

steps.title: Extract Cortisol with Methanol
steps.instruction: Extract cortisol from the powdered hair using HPLC grade methanol.

substeps.instruction: Add 1 mL HPLC grade methanol to each microcentrifuge tube using a motorized pipette controller and serological pipette.
Place tubes on a multi-purpose tube rotator at speed 12 for 24 hours.
Immediately centrifuge samples at 14,000 RPM for 3 minutes after the 24-hour period.
Collect 0.6 mL (600 microliters) of supernatant into a 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube without disturbing the hair pellet.

steps.title: Evaporate Methanol
steps.instruction: Remove methanol from the supernatant using a nitrogen evaporation system (MicroVap) under a fume hood.

substeps.instruction: Turn on the nitrogen tank and place samples on the bed.
Position the nitrogen apparatus so tips are centered over each tube.
Turn on the unit and slowly increase nitrogen flow using the knob until the gauge is at approximately 10 to prevent splashing.
Monitor evaporation, increasing flow as needed; the process takes 45 to 1 hour.
Clean metal pins with alcohol after use.

steps.title: Prepare for Assay
steps.instruction: Thaw and dilute samples according to species before performing the cortisol assay.

substeps.instruction: Allow samples to thaw.
Dilute samples: 1:40 for Capuchins, marmosets, and tamarins; no dilution for Chimpanzees.
Add PBS buffer: 200 micrometers for Capuchins, marmosets, and tamarins; 100 micrometers for Chimpanzees.
Cover tubes with parafilm and store at -20 C until the assay is performed.
Follow the Salimetrics Manual for Salivary Cortisol for the final procedure.
